decision_conditions: Time limit	The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice.Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Approved plans and documentsThe development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Site Location Plan 5653-CA-00-XX-DR-A-00001 P01; Site Demolition Plan 5653-CA-00-00-DR-A-00003 P01; Proposed Site Layout Plan 5653-CA-00-00-DR-A-00050 P05; Units 1-3 GA Floor Plans 5653-CA-00-ZZ-DR-A-00100 P01; Units 4-7 GA Floor Plans 5653-CA-00-ZZ-DR-A-00101 P01; Units 1-3 GA Roof Plans 5653-CA-00-RF-DR-A-00110 P01; Units 4-7 GA Roof Plans 5653-CA-00-RF-DR-A-00111 P01; Proposed Units 1-3 GA Elevations 5653-CA-00-ZZ-DR-A-02100 P01; Proposed Units 4-7 GA Elevations 5653-CA-00-ZZ-DR-A-02101 P01; Units 1-3 GA Sections 5653-CA-00-XX-DR-A-00150 P02; Units 4-7 GA Sections 5653-CA-00-XX-DR-A-00151 P02; Decorative Fence Details 5653-CA-00-XX-DR-A-00300 P2; Typical Paladin Fencing Details 5653-CA-00-XX-DR-A-00301 P01; Typical Cycle Park and Shelter 5653-CA-00-XX-DR-A-00302 P01; Landscape Hard and Soft General Arrangement Plan RG-LD-90 P4; Preliminary Risk Assessment - 20524100-WAT-XX-XX-RP-N-770001_A2_C01; Ground Investigation Report - 205241100-WAT-XX-XX-RP-N-770002_P01_S1; Remediation Strategy - 20524100-WAT-XX-XX-SY-N-770001_P01_S1; Verification Plan included in Remediation Strategy 20524100-WAT-XX-XX-SY-N-770001_P01_S1; Air Quality Assessment, Waterman; Daylight and Sunlight Review Point2; Landscape and Ecological Management Plan, Stantec; Ecological Assessment, Greenspace; Biodiversity Net Gain Report, Greenspace; Energy Strategy, MBA; External Lighting Report, MBA; Fire Safety Strategy, Bureau Veritas; Flood Risk Assessment and Drainage Strategy, Waterman; Archaeological Desk Based Assessment RPS Tetratech; Noise Impact Assessment, Waterman; Preliminary Construction Management Plan, Goodrich; Sustainability Statement, Ensphere; Transport Assessment SLR; Framework Travel Plan, SLR; Delivery & Servicing Management Plan, SLR; Outline Construction Logistics Plan, SLR; Utilities Statement, MBA; Circular Economy Strategy, Ensphere; Site Waste Management Plan, Ensphere; Operational Waste Management Plan, Ensphere; Whole Lifecycle Carbon Assessment, Ensphere; Tree Survey / Tree Constraints Plan, GreenpaceFor information:Planning Statement, TurleyMarket Report, TurleyCommunity Use & Business Relocation Statement, TurleyDesign and Access Statement, ChetwoodsEconomic Benefits Summary Statement, TurleyStatement of Community Involvement, ConcilioSite Audit Report, BNP ParibasReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Electricity substations and pumping station details	Prior to above ground works, full details of the two electricity substations and pumping station shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  Details shall include plans, elevations, sections and materials of the structures.Reason: In order to ensure that the structures have an acceptable appearance and are acceptable in the context of the wide development.

Detailed drawings and sample materials	a. Prior to the completion of superstructure works, details of all the external finishing materials to be used on the façades of the building hereby permitted including for the walls, doors, windows, front entrances, canopies, landscape materials (paving and hard surfacing materials, and any boundary treatments, including edging and planters) rainwater goods, brise soleils and rooflights, handrails, fencing have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. b. Prior to the completion of the external building works, details of, gates and public benches within the development hereby permitted shall be submitted and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. For a. and b. a schedule of materials and their use in the approved scheme is required and samples made available on site if required. A photograph showing all samples to be inspected must be submitted. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details. Reason: In order to ensure that the building has an acceptable external appearance and fire resistance

Place branding	Prior to the completion of the external building works, details of site branding shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.  Signage, subject to advertising consent, shall be informed by the approved details.Reason: In order to ensure that signage is cohesive and clear, and corresponds to the approved materials.

Landscaping and ecological management and monitoring plan	The landscape areas within the development hereby approved shall be managed and monitored strictly in accordance with the approved Landscape and Ecological Management Plan (Ref: 333101256 RG-LD-Claverings LEMP REV A), beginning in the first planting season following completion (or earlier, if applicable).Reason: To ensure that the ecological value of the site is enhanced post development, and to comply with Policies CP30 and CP36 of the Core Strategy, Policies DMD37, DMD80 and DMD81 of the Development Management Document and Policies D4, D8, G4 and G5 of the London Plan.

Biodiversity enhancements	Prior to the completion of superstructure works, details of biodiversity enhancements, to include a minimum of 8 bird and or bat boxes and native and wildlife friendly landscaping (including gaps at the bases of fences to allow hedgehogs to traverse through them), shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the council. The biodiversity enhancements shall thereafter be installed as approved.  Reason: To incorporate biodiversity in and around developments in accordance with Chapter 15 of the NPPF.

Clearance during bird nesting seasonAll areas of hedges, scrub or similar vegetation where birds may nest which are to be removed as part of the development, are to be cleared outside the bird-nesting season (March - August inclusive) or if clearance during the bird-nesting season cannot reasonably be avoided, a suitably qualified ecologist will check the areas to be removed immediately prior to clearance and advise whether nesting birds are present. If active nests are recorded, no vegetation clearance or other works that may disturb active nests shall proceed until all young have fledged the nest.Reason: To ensure that wildlife is not adversely impacted by the proposed development in accordance with national wildlife legislation and in line with CP36 of the Core Strategy. Nesting birds are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act, 1981 (as amended).

Demolition and Construction Management Plan	No development shall take place until a Demolition and/or Construction Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Demolition and/or Construction Management Plan shall be based on the Preliminary Construction Management Plan (October 2024) prepared by Goodrich Consulting LLP and include:Construction Traffic a) photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site;b) map showing routeing of demolition and construction vehicles to/from the site;c) access arrangements to the site;d) wheel cleaning methodology and facilitiesThe development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Plan.Reason: In the interest of highway safety.Environmental Management Plane) Risk assessment of potentially damaging demolition and/or construction activities. f) Identification of "biodiversity protection zones". g) Practical measures (both physical measures and sensitive working practices) to avoid or reduce impacts during construction (may be provided as a set of method statements). h) The location and timing of sensitive works to avoid harm to biodiversity features. i) The times during construction when specialist ecologists need to be present on site to oversee works. j) Responsible persons and lines of communication. k) The role and responsibilities on site of an ecological clerk of works (ECoW) or similarly competent person. l) Use of protective fences, exclusion barriers and warning signs. m) A Japanese knotweed treatment plan.Dust emissionsn) Details of how dust and emissions will be managed during demolition and construction work in accordance with the Mayor of London's supplementary planning guidance 'The Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' The approved Demolition and/or Construction Management Plan shall be adhered to and implemented throughout the demolition and construction stages strictly in accordance with the approved details, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.Reason: To minimise impacts on biodiversity in accordance with Chapter 15 of the NPPF. To protect the local amenity from demolition/construction dust.

External LED Lighting Assessment Report compliance	The development hereby approved shall be implemented in accordance with the approved External LED Lighting Assessment Report prepared by MBA (October 2024) before it is first occupied. The external lighting shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure that the development does not prejudice the amenities of adjoining occupiers and / or the visual amenities of the surrounding area, and to ensure that the development protects community safety.

Secured by DesignThe development (or parts thereof) hereby permitted shall not be occupied until a Certificate of Compliance in accordance with Secured by Design - Homes Guide 2024 (or the relevant Secured by Design Guide(s) or an achieved Crime Prevention Standard) for the development (or parts thereof) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Metropolitan Police or Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall thereafter be installed and permanently retained.Reason: In the interest of creating safer, secure, sustainable communities.

Outline Fire Safety Strategy compliance	The development must be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Fire Strategy Ref. S24053722 - Issue No.3 prepared by Bureau Veritas Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Policies D5 and D12 of London Plan (2021)

Archaeology - Written Scheme of Investigation (Stages 1 and 2)	A. No demolition (except to ground floor slab level of the existing structures) or development shall take place until a stage 1 written scheme of investigation (WSI) has been submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the WSI, no demolition or development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed WSI, and the programme and methodology of site evaluation and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed works.B. If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by stage 1 then for those parts of the site which have archaeological interest a stage 2 WSI shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority in writing. For land that is included within the stage 2 WSI, no demolition/development shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed stage 2 WSI which shall include:a. The statement of significance and research objectives, the programme and methodology of site investigation and recording and the nomination of a competent person(s) or organisation to undertake the agreed worksb. Where appropriate, details of a programme for delivering related positive public benefitsc. The programme for post-investigation assessment and subsequent analysis, publication & dissemination and deposition of resulting material.This part of the condition shall not be discharged until these elements have been fulfilled in accordance with the programme set out in the stage 2 WSI.Reason:

Cycle parkingPrior to first occupation of a unit within the development hereby approved (excluding occupation by any personnel engaged in construction, fitting out or occupation for marketing or display or operations in relation to security) until the details), all long- and short-stay cycle parking shall be provided in accordance with the details provided in the Table 4-3 of the Transport Assessment (4 November 2024) and Drawing refs. 5653-CA-00-00-DR-A-050 P05 and 5653-CA-00-DR-A-00302 P01. The cycle parking facilities shall be retained and maintained for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of cycle parking in accordance with Policy T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), the Council's adopted standards and London Cycling Design Standards Chapter 8.

Delivery and Servicing Management Plan compliance	The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Delivery and Servicing Management Plan Rev. 02 (November 2024) by SLR.Reason: To comply with policy T7 of the London Plan (2021)

Construction Site Waste Management Plan and compliance	The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Site Waste Management Plan Ref.V3 (November 2024) by Ensphere.Reason: To maximise the amount of waste diverted from landfill consistent with the waste hierarchy and to accord with Policy DMD57 of the Development Management Document (2014).

Operational Waste Management Plan and compliance	The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Operational Waste Management Plan Ref. V3 (October 2024) by Ensphere.Reason: To maximise the amount of waste diverted from landfill consistent with the waste hierarchy and to accord with Policy SI 7 of the New London Plan (2021), Policy DMD57 of the Development Management Document (2014).

BREEAM - excellent or higher	A. Each unit of the development hereby approved shall achieve a BREEAM rating of 'Excellent' or higher or an equivalent independent measure of energy performance and sustainability. Where the performance of the development is measured using BREEAM, it shall use reasonable endeavours to achieve not less than the total credits for each of the Energy, Materials and Waste categories in the BREEAM Pre-Assessment hereby approved.B. A post completion certificate (or equivalent certification) confirming that each unit of the development has been completed in accordance with the required BREEAM rating shall be submitted to us for our approval within six months of first occupation of the respective unit.Reason: To ensure the development minimises operational carbon dioxide emissions and achieves the highest levels of sustainable design and construction in accordance with DMD51 of the Development Management Document (2014) and Policy SE2 of the emerging Enfield Local Plan 2019-2041 currently in Examination with the Planning Inspectorate.

Updated Energy and Sustainability Strategy 	A. The development shall be carried out in all respects in accordance with the hereby approved Energy & Sustainability Strategy (P2), October 2024.B. Prior to the occupation of development, an Updated Energy Plan (referred to and defined in the S106 agreement forming part of this permission) to confirm that the development has been built in accordance with the details as approved in the approved Energy Strategy, inclusive of EPC services, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Updated Energy Plan must include Carbon Dioxide Emissions per Unit as currently presented in the approved Energy Strategy.C. Within six months of first occupation, evidence shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority that the development has been registered on the GLA's Be Seen energy monitoring platform.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy SI 2 of the London Plan.

No hazardous materials below flood level	No hazardous materials shall be stored below the flood level of 12.25m A.O.D.Reason: To protect occupant safety and to prevent ground and water contamination.

Flood Management Plan compliance and updated Flood Management PlanPrior to the occupation of the development, an updated Flood Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating:o                 The timings of the onset of flooding, the time it takes for the 1 in 100 year plus climate change event to reach peak flooding, and the duration of floodingo                 The development is provided with a dry access route within the low hazard area of the floodplain (as defined by the Environment Agency's Flood Risk Assessment Guidance for New Development R&D Technical Report FD2320) before the onset of flooding.o                 The Flood Management procedures before, during and after a flood evento                 The duration of occupation in the safe refuge areas is less than 24 hours or as far as practicably possible subject to updated modelling information.The development must be implemented in accordance with the updated Flood Management Plan thereafter.REASON: To minimise flood risk in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy and Policies SI12 of the London Plan, DMD Policy 59, 60 and 62, the SFRA and the NPPF.

Drainage Strategy compliance and Updated Drainage StrategyPrior to the commencement of any construction work (excluding demolition, site investigation works, and other facilitating works), details of the Sustainable Drainage Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority and shall conform with the principles of the Flood Risk Assessment & Drainage Strategy dated March 2025 prepared by Waterman. The Updated Drainage Strategy shall demonstrate that the development achieves greenfield runoff rates and that the proposal assesses the integration of - to the degree possible - further source control measures, including:o	Use of green roofs; and/oro	Use of traditional downpipes to discharge onto adjacent approved source control SuDS features. The details shall include:i) A final detailed SuDS plan including levels, runoff routes and pipe runsii) Sizes, storage volumes, cross-sections, long-sections (where appropriate) and specifications of all the SuDS measures. Calculations demonstrating functionality shall be included where relevant.iii) Further information on the functionality and activation of the source control SuDS features, including demonstration that runoff is discharging onto the surface of the SUDS features to reduce the risk of siltation.iv) A detailed Future Maintenance Management Plan including clear ownership, management and maintenance arrangements.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policies S12 and 13 of the London Plan (2021), Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy (2010), DMD 61 of the Enfield Development Management Plan (2014) and the NPPF (2024).

Non-Road Mobile Machinery	All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/Reason: In the interest of good air quality

Land contamination - foundations works risk assessment, site investigation, remediation strategy (including for unidentified and/or unexpected remediation), verification, and monitoring and maintenance	Any remediation shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Remediation Strategy, 20524100-WAT-XX-XX-SY-N-770001_P01_S1.   1 The development shall not be occupied until a post completion remediation Verification Report, including results of sampling and monitoring carried out, has first been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority demonstrating that the site remediation criteria have been met.2 If during a particular phase of development within the Main Remediation Site contamination that has not previously been identified or unexpected is found to be present in a particular area of the development, then no further development in that area (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out until the developer has submitted an updated addendum remediation strategy specifically for the previously unidentified contamination to the Local Planning Authority detailing how it shall be dealt with and obtained written approval from the Local Planning Authority. The addendum remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved. Reason: To safeguard groundwater quality and human health in accordance with policy 2.1.8 of the London Plan (2016) and CP32 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010).

Acoustic report - mechanical plant	No mechanical plant shall be installed in a unit until an acoustic report, written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from the mechanical plant associated with the respective unit and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the mechanical plant does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest or most noise affected residential property.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance

Sound insulation - buildings/units	Sound insulation of the units shall be in line with the information provided in the acoustic report submitted with the application. The details of the sound insulation for each unit shall be based upon their predicted use and sound emissions and submitted to and approved by the local planning authority prior to occupation.Reason:

Acoustic report - refrigerated vehicles (nighttime only)	No refrigerated vehicles shall be used during night-time hours (2300-0600) until an acoustic report, written in line with the methodology in BS4142:2014+A1 2019, has been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The report must set out the sound level generated from refrigerated vehicles at night and state the noise control measures to be employed to ensure the noise from the refrigerated vehicles plant does not exceed a level of 5dB below the typical measured background noise level measured as L(A)90 15 minutes during operational hours, at the façade of the nearest or most noise affected residential property.Reason: To protect the local amenity from noise and disturbance
